## Korean patterns

Written for Uplika. These are not the lists above translated: a translated English hook reads as an advert in Korean. Use them when the person writes in Korean, fill the brackets with their own specifics, and keep the endings their voice file uses.

| # | Pattern | Example | Use for | Watch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 아직도 [낡은 방법] 하세요? | 아직도 엑셀로 재고 관리하세요? | Calling out a habit the reader recognises in themselves | The habit must be common in this audience, or it reads as an insult |
| 2 | [구체적인 대상]이라면 이것부터 보세요 | 이제 막 스마트스토어 연 분이라면 이것부터 보세요 | Narrowing to the reader who will act | 「직장인이라면」 is too broad to qualify anyone |
| 3 | [행동]했더니 생긴 일 | 한 달 동안 매일 아침 블로그 썼더니 생긴 일 | An experiment with a real cost in time or money | Say what actually happened; a vague 「놀라운 일」 is clickbait |
| 4 | 결론부터 말하면, [답] | 결론부터 말하면, 첫 달 광고는 끄는 게 맞았습니다 | Information posts and blog openings where the reader came for an answer | Give the real answer first, then the reasons |
| 5 | [A] vs [B], 직접 [기간] 써 보고 고른 쪽 | 노션 vs 구글 문서, 직접 석 달 써 보고 고른 쪽 | Comparisons that end with a pick | Name the loser and why; a tie is not an ending |
| 6 | [금액] 쓰고 나서야 알게 된 것 | 광고비 200만 원 쓰고 나서야 알게 된 것 | Trust through a cost the person paid | Only an amount the person really paid and is willing to say |
| 7 | [일] [기간] 하면서 한 번도 안 한 것 | 카페 7년 하면서 한 번도 안 한 것 | Insider experience without a credential | The years must be real |
| 8 | 모르면 손해 보는 [주제] | 모르면 손해 보는 연말정산 공제 하나 | Practical tips with a clear loss | The loss must be concrete; loss framing on every post reads as an advert |
| 9 | [검색창에 치는 질문 그대로]? | 스마트스토어 첫 달 매출 0원, 정상인가요? | Search-led posts and videos | Keep the reader's own wording; tidying it loses the point |
| 10 | [하나]만 바꿨는데 [결과] | 썸네일 글씨만 키웠는데 클릭이 늘었습니다 | One change and its effect | Name the one thing; several changes make it unbelievable |
| 11 | 솔직히 말하면, [인정하기 싫은 것] | 솔직히 말하면, 첫 제품은 제가 봐도 별로였습니다 | A confession that earns attention | The admission has to cost something; a disguised boast reads as fake |
| 12 | [긴 시간] 걸리던 [일], 이제 [짧은 시간]이면 끝납니다 | 반나절 걸리던 견적서, 이제 20분이면 끝납니다 | Process and tool posts where speed is the payoff | A believable gap; an extreme one is read as a lie |
| 13 | [날짜]부터 달라지는 [제도], 지금 할 일 | 다음 달부터 달라지는 배달앱 수수료, 지금 할 일 | A real, checkable change | Real dates only; one invented deadline discounts every later one |
| 14 | [통념]이라고요? 저는 반대로 했습니다 | 매일 올려야 큰다고요? 저는 일주일에 한 번만 올렸습니다 | Contrarian takes | The proof has to follow right away |
| 15 | ...그 말을 듣고 [행동] | ...그 말을 듣고 그날 바로 계약을 취소했습니다 | Stories that start in the middle of the scene | Fill in the setup soon after, or it reads as a mistake |
| 16 | [다들 필요하다는 것] 없어도 됩니다 | 블로그 시작하는 데 비싼 카메라 없어도 됩니다 | Relief: removing a blocker | Put something in its place; that second half is the post |
| 17 | [상황]이면 저장해 두세요 | 이사 앞둔 분이면 저장해 두세요 | Checklists and how-tos people come back to | The post has to be worth coming back to |
| 18 | 내돈내산 [제품] [기간] 써 본 후기 | 내돈내산 무선청소기 석 달 써 본 후기 | Reviews, especially on Naver Blog | Only when the person really paid; a sponsored post says so |
| 19 | [사소한 것] 하나 때문에 [손해] | 계약서 한 줄 때문에 보증금을 못 돌려받았습니다 | Mistakes with a single cause | The cause and the loss must be real |

Writing notes for Korean openings:

- Front-load the hook. Korean puts the verb last, so the words that carry the hook (the number, the reader, the keyword) go first.
- Address the reader by their situation (`이제 막 시작한 분`) rather than `당신`, which reads stiff or confrontational in most posts. Use `여러분` sparingly.
- Avoid translated phrasing such as `~에 대해 알아보겠습니다`, `이것이 바로 ~입니다` and `당신이 몰랐던 ~`. They read as translations or adverts.
- Cut intensifiers that promise without saying anything: `진짜`, `완전`, `대박`, `미쳤다`, `레전드`.
- Endings come from the voice file. Keep one register in a post (해요체, 합니다체 or 반말), never a mix.
- Write numbers the way people say and search them (`석 달`, `200만 원`), and only real ones.
- On Naver Blog the title follows the keyword set's `draftPrompt`; these patterns are for the opening lines of the body.
- On Threads, give the hook a line of its own and break the line after it.
